election_dates.generalSnippet: KRS 118.025: The election of all officers of all governmental units shall be held on the first Tuesday after the first Monday in November.

state_background_check.value: No — Kentucky's constitution excludes convicted felons from office generally (relievable only by a gubernatorial pardon), but the U.S. Constitution's own qualifications for Congress (age, citizenship, residency) can't be added to by any state, so this doesn't reach U.S. House or Senate candidates
state_background_check.snippet: Ky. Const. § 150: "All persons shall be excluded from office who have been, or shall hereafter be, convicted of a felony, or of such high misdemeanor as may be prescribed by law, but such disability may be removed by pardon of the Governor." Congressional qualifications are set exclusively by the U.S. Constitution, confirmed per https://www.everycrsreport.com/reports/R41946.html: "the Framers intended the Constitution to be the exclusive source of qualifications for Members of Congress, and that the Framers thereby 'divested' States of any power to add qualifications."

Ralph is stepping up to bring independent leadership to Washington, lower the cost of living, strengthen Kentucky’s economy, and deliver practical solutions that put Kentucky families first. bio_summary.value: Zach was raised in Lexington and is a ninth-generation Kentuckian. His family roots trace back to the mid-1700s in Shelby and Henry County. Until his parents’ generation, every ancestor on that side of the family earned their living the same way: farming. Zach went to Stanford University and after college, worked as an eighth grade English teacher in the Mississippi Delta, as a part of the Teach For America program. He then attended the University of Michigan Law School, where he made the decision to serve his country and commissioned as an officer in the United States Navy Judge Advocate General’s (JAG) Corps.

bio_summary.value: My name is Jay J Bowman (the middle name is only an initial; I'm convinced my parents could not agree on their children's names and just gave them initials). I was born in Michigan and grew up in Utah. I remember the winters, the vast forest of green surrounding the lake of our small town in Michigan. My parents moved to Salt Lake City when I was 8 years old. Utah was a wonderful place to grow up. I enjoyed hunting, fishing, skiing, and love the mountains and deserts of the state.

bio_summary.value: Pete Lynch decided to get his PhD in American Politics after reading research showing that Congress represents the rich instead of average Americans (Gilens and Page 2014). He wanted to understand why our government favors the rich and what it would take to make Congress work for average Americans. He has taught politics courses at the University of Kentucky, Centre College, and Eastern Kentucky University, giving him first-hand experience explaining how government works—or doesn’t work—for average Americans.
